firefighter-helmet.context: A side view of a firefighter helmet with a rounded crown, a shield plate on the front and a long brim at the back. Used for fire service pages, protective gear lists and rescue team branding.

fire-axe.context: A firefighter's axe drawn at an angle with a curved blade on one side of the head and a pointed pick on the other. Used for forcible entry, fire service tool lists and rescue equipment.

halligan-bar.context: A long forcible-entry bar with a forked claw at one end and an adze and pick at the other. Used for fire service tool lists and breaking open doors in rescues.

pike-pole.context: A long pole with a pointed tip and a curved hook just behind it. Used by firefighters to pull down ceilings and walls, and in fire service equipment lists.

fire-hose-coupling.context: Two hose couplings facing each other with a short hose stub leaving each outer side. Used for connecting hoses, water supply diagrams and fire service equipment.

rolled-fire-hose.context: A flat fire hose wound into a tight spiral disc with a small coupling at its edge. Used for hose storage, fire equipment inventories and station checklists.

fire-hose-wye.context: A Y-shaped hose fitting with one inlet splitting into two outlets, each with a small lever valve. Used to show a hose line dividing into two lines.

fire-hose-spray.context: A fire hose nozzle held level with a wide fan of water spraying out of it. Used for fire suppression, water stream and hose training content.

fire-bucket.context: A cone-bottomed red-style fire bucket with a carry handle and a small flame badge. Used for sand or water buckets kept on walls in buildings and workshops.

fire-beater.context: A long-handled wildfire beater with a flat rubber mat at the end. Used for beating out grass and brush fires and in wildland fire tool lists.

wildfire-backpack-pump.context: A water bladder worn as a backpack with a hose leading to a hand-held slide pump. Used for wildland firefighting gear and forest fire crews.

pulaski-axe.context: A wildland tool with an axe blade on one side of the head and a flat adze on the other. Used for digging fire lines and cutting roots and brush.

fire-rake.context: A wide-bladed wildland rake with a row of tines along one edge. Used for scraping a fire line down to bare soil and in wildfire tool lists.

breathing-apparatus.context: An air cylinder with a hose leading to a full-face mask. Used for firefighter breathing gear, smoke entry and confined-space safety content.

turnout-coat.context: A firefighter's protective coat with a high collar, front clasps and reflective bands on the body and sleeves. Used for fire service clothing and protective equipment.

fire-alarm-strobe.context: A wall-mounted horn and strobe box with speaker dots and a flashing lens with rays above it. Used for alarm systems, building safety plans and alert devices.

heat-detector.context: A low round ceiling detector with wavy heat lines rising toward it. Used for fire detection systems in kitchens, garages and other places where smoke detectors misfire.

carbon-monoxide-detector.context: A wall detector box with the letters CO on its display and a row of vent dots below. Used for home safety, gas leak warnings and building inspection content.

fire-door.context: A heavy door with a small glass window, a handle and a flame badge on the leaf. Used for building safety plans, fire exits and compliance checklists.

co2-fire-extinguisher.context: An extinguisher cylinder with a long flared discharge horn on a hose. Used for electrical fire safety and equipment rooms.

wheeled-fire-extinguisher.context: A large extinguisher cylinder on a two-wheeled trolley with a pull handle. Used for airports, factories and workshops where a bigger unit must be moved.

fire-extinguisher-ball.context: A round ball-shaped extinguisher with a flame mark, resting in a wall cradle. Used for automatic or throwable fire suppression devices in small rooms.

fire-hose-cabinet.context: A wall cabinet with a coiled hose visible behind its door. Used for building fire protection, hose reel locations and safety maps.

fire-department-connection.context: A twin-inlet hose connection with two round capped inlets joined to a single pipe. Used on building exteriors to feed water to sprinklers and standpipes.

fire-hydrant-wrench.context: A wrench with a pentagon socket head on a long straight handle. Used for opening street hydrants and in water utility and fire service tool lists.

portable-fire-pump.context: A small engine-driven pump on a tube frame with a discharge outlet on top. Used for wildland and rural firefighting and for moving water from ponds and tanks.

fire-monitor-nozzle.context: A deck-mounted water cannon on a short riser with a long barrel shooting a jet. Used for fire boats, industrial plants and large fire suppression.

fire-alarm-control-panel.context: A wall panel with a small screen, a row of zone lights and two buttons. Used for building alarm systems, security rooms and fire safety inspections.

flammable-storage-cabinet.context: A tall double-door safety cabinet with a flame mark on one door and short legs. Used for storing solvents, fuels and paints in workshops and laboratories.

smoke-ejector-fan.context: A portable fan in a square housing blowing three lines of air forward. Used by firefighters to clear smoke and heat out of a building.

portable-water-tank.context: An open-top folding water tank with water inside and a hose running in over the rim. Used for temporary water supply at rural and wildland fires.

sprinkler-riser.context: A vertical sprinkler pipe with a pressure gauge and a handwheel valve beside it. Used for building fire protection plans and plant room maintenance.

street-fire-alarm-box.context: An old street fire alarm box with a gabled top, a pull handle and a pedestal post. Used for historic fire service themes and street emergency call points.

fire-engine-pump-panel.context: A fire engine pump panel with two round gauges above a row of lever handles. Used for pump operator training and fire truck equipment diagrams.

fire-service-cross.context: An eight-pointed cross with flared notched arms and a small disc at the centre. Used as a fire service badge or emblem for brigades and memorials.

helicopter-water-bucket.context: A helicopter carrying a bucket on a long line, with drops falling from the bucket. Used for aerial firefighting and wildfire water drops.

fire-pole.context: A vertical sliding pole passing through a gap between two floor slabs. Used for fire station themes and for speed of response.

roof-ladder.context: A straight ladder with two folding hooks at the top that catch on a roof ridge. Used for firefighter roof access and rescue training.

house-fire.context: A small house with a flame inside and a larger flame rising behind the roof. Used for home fire warnings, insurance claims and fire safety content.

high-rise-fire.context: A tall tower block with a grid of windows and a flame rising from its upper floors. Used for tower fire safety, evacuation and high-rise rescue content.

grease-fire.context: A frying pan with a tall flame rising out of it. Used for kitchen fire warnings and cooking safety advice.

electrical-fire.context: A plug with two prongs and a flame rising from its connection. Used for wiring hazards, appliance safety and fire prevention advice.

lithium-battery-fire.context: A swollen battery cell with a plus mark and a flame rising from its top. Used for battery safety notices, e-bike and phone charging warnings.

overloaded-socket.context: A multi-plug adapter with three cords fanning out and a spark jumping from its edge. Used for warnings about too many devices on one outlet.

frayed-wire.context: An electrical cord with torn insulation and three bare strands spreading from its end. Used for electrical hazard warnings and repair notices.

chimney-fire.context: A house roof with a chimney and a flame rising from its top with sparks nearby. Used for winter heating safety and chimney maintenance advice.

prescribed-burn.context: A person walking with a drip torch behind a low line of flames moving over the ground. Used for controlled burn programs and land management.

firebreak.context: Flames on the left, a bare cleared strip in the middle and a tree on the right. Used for wildfire containment and defensible space planning.

fire-shelter.context: A low foil emergency shelter lying on the ground with crinkled folds. Used as a last-resort wildland survival symbol for firefighters.

fire-tornado.context: A spinning funnel of narrowing bands with a flame at its base. Used for extreme wildfire behavior and fire whirl warnings.

burned-forest.context: Three bare blackened trunks with broken branch stubs standing on scorched ground. Used for wildfire aftermath, damage reports and recovery topics.

flying-embers.context: Glowing ember specks carried on wind lines toward the roof of a house. Used for ember attack and wildfire home protection warnings.

fire-lane-sign.context: A post-mounted sign with two lines of lettering and a circle with a slash, marking a no-parking fire lane. Used for parking rules and emergency access routes.

smokejumper.context: A firefighter hanging under an open parachute canopy. Used for aerial wildland firefighting and remote fire crews.

fire-chief.context: The front view of a firefighter in a helmet with a shield badge and a coat collar. Used for fire service leadership, command and officer roles.

fire-warden.context: A person in a vest with a flame badge, holding a clipboard and pointing the way. Used for evacuation leaders and floor safety officers.

fire-drill.context: Two small figures walking toward an open door with a bell above it. Used for evacuation practice, workplace safety and school emergency procedures.

fire-evacuation-plan.context: A framed floor plan with a wall outline, a you-are-here dot and a route arrow to the exit. Used for escape maps on building walls.

fireman-carry.context: A rescuer standing with another person draped across the shoulders. Used for rescue techniques, first aid training and carrying casualties.

crawl-under-smoke.context: A person crawling on hands and knees beneath two wavy layers of smoke. Used for fire escape advice telling people to stay low.

hydraulic-rescue-spreader.context: A rescue spreader with two long pointed jaw arms opening like a beak and a hose at the back. Used for car crash extrication and heavy rescue tool lists.

lifting-air-bag.context: A flat inflatable cushion under a heavy load with an upward arrow. Used for lifting vehicles and debris during rescue work.

confined-space-tripod.context: A rescue tripod with a pulley at its top and a rope hanging down toward a round opening. Used for manhole, tank and trench entry rescue.

figure-eight-descender.context: A metal figure-eight device with a large lower ring and a smaller upper ring. Used for rappelling, abseiling and rope rescue gear.

avalanche-probe.context: A long jointed probe pole with a ring handle pushed down into a snow mound. Used for avalanche rescue, ski patrol and backcountry safety.

search-and-rescue-dog.context: A dog in a cross-marked harness vest standing with its nose to the ground. Used for disaster search teams and missing person searches.

hoist-rescue.context: A helicopter hovering with a winch cable lowering a rescuer who holds a second person. Used for sea, mountain and flood helicopter rescues.

rescue-cutoff-saw.context: A hand-held cut-off saw with a round blade under a guard, an engine body and a top handle. Used for cutting through metal and concrete during rescues.

emergency-hammer.context: A car escape hammer with a pointed tip on the head and a belt-cutter slot in the handle. Used for car safety kits and vehicle escape instructions.

head-immobilizer.context: A head support board with two foam side blocks, a head shape and straps. Used for spinal injury care and paramedic equipment.

rubble-search-camera.context: A small camera on a telescopic pole pushed into the gap between two slabs of rubble. Used for collapsed building searches.

rescue-toboggan.context: A boat-shaped rescue sled with rope handles at both ends and a patient strapped in. Used for ski patrol and mountain rescue.

breeches-buoy.context: A life ring hanging from a pulley that runs along a taut rope line. Used for ship-to-shore and cliff rescues.

trench-shoring.context: A narrow trench in cross-section with two wall panels braced apart by screw struts. Used for excavation safety and trench rescue.

mine-rescuer.context: A rescuer in a hard hat with a head lamp and a breathing pack on the chest. Used for underground rescue teams and mine safety.

first-aider.context: A person with an armband carrying a small first-aid bag marked with a plus. Used for volunteer first responders and workplace first aid roles.

rescue-swimmer-tow.context: A swimmer towing a second person on their back across the water. Used for lifeguard skills, water rescue and drowning prevention.

aed-wall-cabinet.context: A wall cabinet with a heart and lightning bolt mark on its front. Used for public defibrillator locations and cardiac emergency maps.

air-ambulance-plane.context: A plane seen from above with a plus sign beside it. Used for medical flights, patient transfer and air ambulance services.
